title: Let a player play on a stand-in profile while another server still holds their save
observation: Profiles were opened and saved with one UpdateAsync that checks a session lock. In a Studio test with an in-memory store, a fresh lock planted by 'another server' made this server refuse to open the profile; after five tries (16 s) the player kept playing on a blank stand-in, earned 18 Shinies from a raid while purchases were refused, and the stored profile stayed untouched. When the other lock was released, a background retry opened the real profile within 20 s and added the earnings (525 + 18 = 543). Separately, a crashed server's stale lock was taken over and its late save was refused, so newer data survived.
recommendation: Check a session lock inside every UpdateAsync (refuse writes when the lock is not yours), let players start at once on a stand-in profile, block purchases until the real profile is open, and merge only earned currency and stats when it opens.
applies_when: A game saves currency or purchases per player
Players can rejoin quickly or be in two servers
limits: Tested on an in-memory DataStore stand-in in Studio, not Roblox's live DataStore
Lock timings (180 s stale, 20 s retry) are this game's choices, not measured optima

evidence.detail: Section 23: the planted-lock rejoin test and the automated stale-lock and refused-late-save tests.
